_note: Rhode Island security-deposit rules, retrieved verbatim from the R.I. General Assembly statute server (webserver.rilegislature.gov), R.I. Gen. Laws Title 34 Chapter 18 (Residential Landlord and Tenant Act), § 34-18-19 (Security deposits), retrieved 2026-06-20. § 34-18-19(a): a deposit may not exceed one month's periodic rent. § 34-18-19(b): within 20 days of the later of termination / delivery of possession / forwarding address, the landlord must deliver an itemized notice and the balance. § 34-18-19(c): wrongful withholding exposes the landlord to twice the amount withheld plus attorney fees. RI has no statutory interest-on-deposit requirement in § 34-18-19, so no interest rule is asserted. ALL rules status=draft-unverified: must be reviewed by a Rhode Island tenant attorney / legal-aid clinic before public conclusions.

rules.title: Security deposit exceeds one month's rent
rules.description: Per R.I. Gen. Laws § 34-18-19(a), a landlord may not demand or receive a security deposit (however it is labeled) greater than one month's periodic rent. A clause demanding two months, or first + last + a deposit on top, exceeds the statutory cap as to the excess.
rules.tenant_explainer: In Rhode Island your security deposit can't be more than one month's rent, no matter what the lease calls it. If it asks for two months — or first, last, and a deposit on top — the extra isn't allowed.

citations.label: R.I. Gen. Laws § 34-18-19(a)
citations.quote: A landlord may not demand or receive a security deposit, however denominated, in an amount or value in excess of one month’s periodic rent.

rules.title: No itemized return of the deposit within 20 days
rules.description: Per R.I. Gen. Laws § 34-18-19(b), within 20 days after the later of termination, delivery of possession, or the tenant's giving a forwarding address, the landlord must deliver an itemized written notice of any deductions and return the balance. A clause setting a longer return window, or waiving itemization, conflicts with the statute.
rules.tenant_explainer: After you move out and give a forwarding address, the landlord has 20 days to send you an itemized list of any deductions and return the rest. A lease that says they get 30, 45, or 60 days — or that they don't have to itemize — isn't enforceable.

citations.label: R.I. Gen. Laws § 34-18-19(b)
citations.quote: The landlord shall deliver the notice, together with the amount of the security deposit due to the tenant, within twenty (20) days after the later of either termination of the tenancy, delivery of possession, or the tenant’s providing the landlord with a forwarding address for the purpose of receiving the security deposit.

rules.title: Non-refundable security deposit
rules.description: Under R.I. Gen. Laws § 34-18-19 a security deposit must be returned, less itemized lawful deductions, within 20 days (§ 34-18-19(b)); wrongful withholding exposes the landlord to twice the amount withheld plus attorney fees (§ 34-18-19(c)). Labeling the deposit 'non-refundable' contradicts that scheme and is unenforceable.
rules.tenant_explainer: A deposit isn't a fee — calling it 'non-refundable' doesn't make it so. You're owed it back (minus any itemized real deductions), and if the landlord wrongfully keeps it you can recover twice the amount plus attorney fees.

citations.label: R.I. Gen. Laws § 34-18-19(c)
citations.quote: the tenant may recover the amount due him or her, together with damages in an amount equal to twice the amount wrongfully withheld, and reasonable attorney fees.
